Chapter 10: The Challenge of Change — Adapting to New Beginnings.
Change. It's that one thing you can count on, especially for a child in foster care. Imagine what it's like—every new home means a whole new world: different school, new rules, faces you’ve never seen before. The boy learns, pretty quickly, that he’s got to adapt. He gets good at reading a room, picking up on what’s expected, and figuring out how to fit in.
But honestly, it's exhausting. The fear of making a mistake, of slipping up, is always there.
There’s a special kind of anxiety that comes with having to start over again and again. He worries—will he fit in this time? What if he says the wrong thing? What if people just don’t accept him? So, he makes himself useful, tries to stay out of trouble, and does his best to blend in.
Most folks have no idea how much energy it takes to always be on guard, to never really let your true self show.
Yet, not all changes are bad. Sometimes, there’s a foster family that actually feels like a safe place. Or maybe a school where he manages to make a friend. Sometimes, a staff member notices him, asks how he’s doing, and means it. Those moments—they offer hope. A little sign that maybe, just maybe, things are turning around. But he’s careful. He knows not to get too comfortable, because everything can change in a heartbeat.
Of course, there are setbacks. A placement comes to a sudden end, or a simple misunderstanding spirals into bigger trouble. Maybe a friend he’s just gotten close to moves away. Every loss is a reminder of how fragile stability really is.
Over time, the boy learns to grieve these changes, but he also finds ways to look for the hidden opportunities each new chapter brings.
Gradually, it starts to make sense—change doesn’t always have to be scary. It can be a chance to grow. To learn something new. To meet someone unexpected. The process is never easy, and it never feels simple. But bit by bit, he learns that resilience is built one day at a time, just by being willing to keep trying, no matter how many fresh starts life throws his way.
